subject: Dedicated capacity — pricing follow-up & GPU/throughput qualification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme call recap — dedicated capacity interest (GPU / throughput q's)

Quick recap from today’s call with Jordan / Priya at Acme AI. Main points: they are evaluating Dedicated capacity for productionizing a multi-tenant chat product with strict latency SLAs and predictable unit economics.

Key qualification items we need to confirm before sending a preliminary quote: 
- Estimated monthly token volume: they said 200M–1B tokens/month, currently trending ~350M but expecting growth if trials go well.
- Target unit cost: they asked for target pricing in the ballpark of $100–$200 per 1M tokens for the dedicated setup (they referenced target $/1M tokens).
- Preferred GPUs: mentioned wanting H100-class performance but concerned about cost; open to A100 80GB if it meets throughput.
- Desired reserved capacity: initial ask was 2–4 GPUs, but throughput targets implied they may need more (see below).
- Throughput / latency: they need ~30–50 tokens/sec per request P95 for chat; peak concurrent sessions ~120–200; expected average seq length ~150 tokens.

Action items (internal):
- Marcus: run model throughput sims for both A100 80GB and H100 (quantized 4-bit and 8-bit paths) for a ~7B chat model with avg seq=150 and KV cache load. Provide steady-state qps and tokens/sec per GPU.
- Vanessa: draft a pricing scenario for 2x, 4x, and 8x reserved configurations showing $/1M token equivalent (amortized infra + SW + support) and include canary/burst options.
- Neha: pull their recent usage snapshot they shared (we received acme_usage_snapshot-apr2027.csv) and map to monthly tokens and concurrency.

I’ll follow up with Jordan/Priya once we have the sim numbers and the initial pricing scenarios.

Thanks — Marissa

Jordan / Priya — thanks again for the call. Please see the two quick things we discussed below and a proposed next step for a short follow-up call: 

1) Clarifying volumes & target economics
- You indicated current production is ~350M tokens/month, with an optimistic growth plan to ~700M within 6 months if the pilot succeeds.
- Target unit economics mentioned on the call: $100–$150 / 1M tokens (Procurement goal was <= $150).

2) GPU / reserved capacity thoughts we want to validate
- GPUs: H100 gives better peak token throughput for large models; A100 (80GB) can be significantly cheaper if quantized execution is acceptable. We’ll run throughput sims for both.
- Reserved size: you mentioned 2–4 GPUs to start; depending on tokens/sec and concurrency that may map to 4–8 GPUs for predictable latency.

Next step: Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up later this week so we can present our throughput sims and two pricing scenarios (conservative and aggressive)? I can get Marcus & Vanessa on the call to walk through numbers.

Proposed times (PST): Wed 14 Apr 11:00–11:30, Thu 15 Apr 10:00–10:30, Fri 16 Apr 09:00–09:30. Let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Marissa — Wed/Thu windows look good; we’ll take Thu 15 Apr 10:00 PST (confirmed). A couple of clarifying data points ahead of your sims: 

- Typical concurrent chat sessions during peaks: 150–180 (mostly 1–2 requests/min per session).
- Avg sequence length: 150 tokens; typical prompt prefix ~60 tokens + model response ~90 tokens.
- Batchability: our app has relatively low batching opportunity at request time because of interactive UX, so per-request latency matters more than long-form throughput.
- Budget guidance: procurement is looking for committed pricing for reserved capacity. Their headcount expected to approve capex ~ $18k–$30k/mo depending on hardware choice and clear unit economics. They asked us: what does that map to in $/1M tokens for 2x vs 4x vs 8x reserved configs?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@acme.ai>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — pricing follow-up & GPU/throughput qualification

Jordan / Priya — thanks for the clarification and for confirming Thursday’s call (we’ll send the calendar invite). Quick preview of what we’ll present on Thu: 

1) Throughput sims (Marcus) — summary:
- A100 80GB (fp16 / 8-bit quant path): ~8.5k tokens/sec per GPU steady-state for our reference 7B chat model with KV cache and avg seq=150 (interactive load). That maps to ~510k tokens/hr per GPU (~12.2M tokens/day).
- H100 (fp16 / 4-bit quant path): ~13.0k tokens/sec per GPU steady-state (~780k tokens/hr). H100 increases throughput ~1.5x vs A100 in our tests for this model/stack.

2) Mapping to reserved configs and token economics (Vanessa) — headline scenarios (monthly amortized):
- 2x A100: supports ~1.0–1.2M tokens/hr peak (conservative); roughly maps to ~720M tokens/month sustained at 60% utilization; implied cost ~ $210 / 1M tokens (includes infra + SW + 24x7 support + reserved discount) — above your procurement target.
- 4x A100: supports ~2.0–2.4M tokens/hr; ~1.4B tokens/month at 60% util; implied cost ~ $130 / 1M tokens (closer to target).
- 2x H100: supports ~1.5–1.6M tokens/hr; ~960M tokens/month at 60% util; implied cost ~ $260 / 1M tokens (H100 hardware premium).
- 4x H100: supports ~3.0M tokens/hr; ~1.9B tokens/month at 60% util; implied cost ~ $160 / 1M tokens (still above target but better unit economics at scale).

Notes & tradeoffs:
- If your budget ceiling is ~$18k–$30k/mo, the 4x A100 scenario with committed reserved pricing is the most likely fit to hit <= $150 / 1M tokens.
- H100 delivers headroom for peak latency and extreme burst, but ops cost + instance price push $/1M up unless you commit larger reserved pools.
- We can offer burst capacity options (on-demand GPUs) for short spikes and automated fallback to smaller model variants to preserve latency and reduce cost.

Next steps before Thursday’s call: 
- Marcus to attach the sim logs and per-GPU qps/tokens report.
- Vanessa to attach the draft pricing scenarios (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf) with line-item math so procurement can validate.
- Jordan / Priya: if you can confirm target committed monthly spend (pick a firm number or range within the $18k–$30k band), we’ll make the pricing slide more concrete for procurement.

I’ll send the calendar invite for Thu 15 Apr 10:00 PST and include an agenda and the two attachments. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
